words.gloss: embryo; descent, entry (avakrānti: the entry of the soul and development of the embryo); body-section (śārīra)

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम गर्भावक्रान्ति शारीर की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Śārīra (the section on the body) called Garbhāvakrānti, the descent (entry) of the embryo.
notes: Stock opening formula (atha ataḥ ... vyākhyāsyāmaḥ). Printed -krāṃti- is anusvāra for n (orthography). 'Garbhāvakrānti' is the title of the chapter; 'descent/entry of the embryo' is the literal sense.

words.gloss: in the receptacle (āśaya: womb, garbhāśaya; standard)
by ārtava (menstrual fluid, the female reproductive fluid; standard)
unclear: probably 'immediately, at once' (anu-akṣa); sense uncertain
passion; beginning with; afflictions (kleśa); sway, control; following

hindi: जब पुराना रज चला जाता है और नया रज स्थित हो जाता है, गर्भ के आशय यानी गर्भाशय में और मार्ग में शुद्धता होती है, तब बीज के रूप वाला, विकार रहित शुक्र यानी पुरुष का वीर्य, विकार रहित वायु से प्रेरित, अन्य महाभूतों से अनुगत, आर्तव यानी स्त्री के रज से मिला हुआ, सम्भवतः तुरन्त ही, राग आदि क्लेशों के वश में चलने वाले, अपने कर्म से प्रेरित, मन के समान वेग वाले जीव से संयुक्त होकर गर्भाशय में पहुँचता है।
english: When the old rajas (menstrual blood) has gone, the new one is established, and the receptacle of the embryo (the womb, garbhāśaya) and the passage are clean, the śukra (semen), in the form of seed, unaltered, impelled by unaltered wind (vāyu), followed by the other great elements (mahābhūta), mingled with ārtava (menstrual fluid), probably at once, and joined with the jīva (the living soul) - which follows the sway of the afflictions beginning with passion, is impelled by its own action (karma) and is swift as the mind - goes to the womb.

text_flags.why: possible: the anusvāra before nu is not required (vaśa + anuvartin = vaśānuvartin)

notes: One long sentence, absolute locatives first (gate ... avasthite ... śuddhe), then the subject śukra with its qualifiers. 'anvakṣam' is not certain (taken as anu-akṣa 'at once'; the hedge 'probably' is in the translations); alternative senses not excluded. 'abhisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ' is read as agreeing with śukra. Reading: 'rajasinave' = rajasi + nave. 'sva-karma-coditena', 'manojavena' are qualifiers of jīva. Identification (modern equivalents): rajas = menstrual blood (standard, in this context; elsewhere also a guṇa); śukra = semen (standard); ārtava = menstrual fluid, the female reproductive fluid (standard); garbhāśaya = womb (standard); jīva = living soul (doctrinal, no modern equivalent).
lines_deva: गते पुराणे रजसिनवे ऽवस्थिते शुद्धे गर्भस्याशये मार्गे च बीजात्मना शुक्रमविकृतमविकृतेन वायुना प्रेरितमन्यैश्च महाभूतैरनुगतमार्तवेनाभिमूर्च्छितमन्वक्षमेव रागादिक्लेशवशांनुवर्तिना स्वकर्मचोदितेन मनोजवेन जीवेनाभिसंसृष्टं गर्भाशयमुपयाति
lines_iast: gate purāṇe rajasinave 'vasthite śuddhe garbhasyāśaye mārge ca bījātmanā śukramavikṛtamavikṛtena vāyunā preritamanyaiśca mahābhūtairanugatamārtavenābhimūrcchitamanvakṣameva rāgādikleśavaśāṃnuvartinā svakarmacoditena manojavena jīvenābhisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ garbhāśayamupayāti

hindi: कार्यों के कारण का अनुसरण करने के कारण वह उसी के स्वभाव को प्राप्त होता है।
english: And because effects follow their causes, it attains the nature of that (cause).

text_flags.why: possible: the print has a run of three t and lacks the 'a' of tat; the sense requires āt + tat-svabhāvatām

notes: The subject (the embryo, from line 2 (card 2)) is not stated; 'it' is understood. Split follows the corrected reading; the printed form is kept in src.

words.gloss: napuṃsaka (a person neither male nor female)

hindi: और इसी कारण से शुक्र की अधिकता से पुरुष, आर्तव की अधिकता से स्त्री और उन दोनों की समता से नपुंसक।
english: And for that very reason: a male from the abundance of śukra (semen), a female from the abundance of ārtava (menstrual fluid), a napuṃsaka (neither male nor female) from the equality of the two.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated (a verb such as 'arises' is carried from the sense and is not supplied in the translation). The printed line runs words together (bāhulyātpumānārtavasyabāhulyātstrī); this is a spacing habit, not a typo. napuṃsaka is the third category (lit. 'not male'); no single modern equivalent is asserted.
lines_deva: ततएव च शुक्रस्य बाहुल्यात्पुमानार्तवस्यबाहुल्यात्स्त्री तयोः साम्येन नपुंसकं
lines_iast: tataeva ca śukrasya bāhulyātpumānārtavasyabāhulyātstrī tayoḥ sāmyena napuṃsakaṃ

words.gloss: śukra and ārtava (semen and menstrual fluid)

hindi: शुक्र और आर्तव के वायु से टुकड़ों में विभक्त हो जाने पर विभाग के अनुसार सन्तानों की उत्पत्ति होती है।
english: When śukra and ārtava (semen and menstrual fluid) are split into pieces by anila (Vāta), there is the origin of offspring according to the divisions.
notes: Hindi 'होती है' renders the nominal sentence 'utpattiḥ' (copula understood). The text says 'offspring' in the plural; no count is stated or added. Token 4 fuses yathāvibhāgam + apatyānām + utpattiḥ (printed with no spaces).

hindi: विकृत होने पर अन्य योनि के आकारों की।
english: When vitiated: of the forms of other wombs.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue line 5 (card 5) (utpattiḥ, 'origin', is carried over), so the full sense would be 'when (they are) vitiated, the origin of those with forms of other wombs'; no verb or noun is supplied in the translation. 'viyoni' is read as 'other/different womb'; whether this means animal-like forms is not stated and is not added. What is vitiated (śukra and ārtava from 5, or the vāyu) is not stated.

words.gloss: just now; taken; whose foetus (she who has just conceived)

hindi: अब सद्यः गर्भ धारण की हुई स्त्री का लक्षण: योनि द्वारा बीज का ग्रहण, तृप्ति, भारीपन, फड़कना और शुक्र तथा आर्तव का अनुबन्ध।
english: Now the sign of a woman who has just conceived: the taking in of the seed by the yoni (vagina), satisfaction, heaviness, throbbing, and the continued connection of śukra and ārtava.

text_flags.why: spacing: two words run together (atha + nāryāḥ); certain

notes: 'nāryāḥ' read as gen. sg. of nārī 'woman'. 'yonyā' is read as instrumental ('by the yoni'); a genitive yonyāḥ 'of the yoni' is possible, and the sense changes little. 'gurimā' is nom. sg. of the masc. stem gurimān (usually garimān); it stands in a list of signs. 'sphuraṇam' read as a separate word (no sandhi needed after gurimā). Identification: yoni = vagina, female genital tract (standard).
lines_deva: अथनार्याः सद्योगृहीतगर्भायाश्च लिंगं योन्या बीजग्रहणं तृप्तिर्गुरिमास्फुरणं शुक्रार्तवयोरनुबंधश्च
lines_iast: athanāryāḥ sadyogṛhītagarbhāyāśca liṃgaṃ yonyā bījagrahaṇaṃ tṛptirgurimāsphuraṇaṃ śukrārtavayoranubaṃdhaśca

words.gloss: unclear (printed form; possibly 'great joy' or 'joy', mahā-harṣa/praharṣa)
unclear: printed hṛllābha; probably hṛllāsa, nausea
heart; distress, pain (hṛdaya: the heart; standard)

hindi: इसी प्रकार, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अत्यन्त हर्ष, जी मिचलाना, तन्द्रा, अंगों की शिथिलता, प्रसेक यानी बहाव, हृदय की पीड़ा, थकावट और प्यास।
english: Likewise, on a conjectural reading: great joy, nausea, drowsiness, limb-weariness, flow (praseka), heart-distress, exhaustion and thirst.

text_flags.why: possible: 'maharṣaḥ' is not a fitting word in a list of signs; harṣa-type word suspected; reading uncertain
possible: hṛllāsa 'nausea' is the usual word in such lists; bha/sa confusion; reading uncertain
possible: 'hṛdayanpathā' is not a word; vyathā 'distress' fits the sense; vy/np confusion

notes: Three doubtful words in this list of signs of early pregnancy; the printed forms are kept in src and the translations are marked 'on a conjectural reading'. Only 'maharṣaḥ' is the least sure (the first member could be a noun for joy or horripilation); do not rely on it. 'prasekaḥ' is 'flow, trickling' (no noun supplied). 'aṅga-sādaḥ' is a compound of aṅga + sāda (the print has 'aṃgasādaḥpraseko' joined). Identification: hṛdaya = heart (standard).
lines_deva: तथा महर्षो हृल्लाभस्तंद्राऽंगसादःप्रसेको हृदयन्पथा ग्लानिः पिपासा च
lines_iast: tathā maharṣo hṛllābhastaṃdrā'ṃgasādaḥpraseko hṛdayanpathā glāniḥ pipāsā ca

words.gloss: manifest; whose foetus (she whose pregnancy has become manifest)
weak, faint; eye; voice; state of being

hindi: किन्तु क्रम से, जिसका गर्भ प्रकट हो चुका है उसमें, अनुमानित पाठ पर कुक्षि का ही भारीपन, आँखों और स्वर की क्षीणता, आँख और रोम की सन्तुलनता, जिसका अर्थ अस्पष्ट है,, निद्रा, जम्हाई, मूर्च्छा, उलटी, अरुचि, पैरों की सूजन और खट्टे में अभिलाषा, और उन विविध भावों में।
english: But gradually, in a woman whose pregnancy has become manifest: heaviness of the belly (kukṣi) alone, on a conjectural reading, weakness of eye and voice, balancing (saṃtulana) of eye and hair (sense unclear), sleep, yawning, fainting, vomiting (chardi), distaste for food, swelling of the feet, and craving for the sour, in those various states.

text_flags.why: possible: the print has an extra 'au' after mātra; kukṣi-mātra-gauravam 'heaviness of the belly alone' fits; alternative reading not excluded

notes: Two uncertain items: (1) 'kukṣimātra-gauravam' (print 'kukṣimātraugauravaṃ'): see text_flags; (2) 'akṣi-roma-saṃtulanam' has no clear sense; it is translated literally and its meaning is not asserted. 'kṣāmanetrasvaratā' is read as kṣāma-netra-svara-tā 'weakness of eyes and voice'; the sense of 'tā' with this compound is not secure. The closing 'iti' (here 'thus', ending the list) is shown in notes only. 'amle' loc. 'for the sour (taste)'; no noun like 'things' added. The print runs words together without spaces: vyaktagarbhāyāḥkukṣi-, pādaśopho'mle'bhilāṣasteṣu. Identification: chardi = vomiting; aruci = loss of taste for food (anorexia); śopha = swelling (oedema) (all standard).
lines_deva: क्रमेण तु व्यक्तगर्भायाःकुक्षिमात्रौगौरवं क्षामनेत्रस्वरताऽक्षिरोमसंतुलनं निद्रा जृंभणं मूर्च्छाछर्दिररुचिः पादशोफोऽम्लेऽभिलाषस्तेषु चोच्चावचेषु भावेष्विति
lines_iast: krameṇa tu vyaktagarbhāyāḥkukṣimātraugauravaṃ kṣāmanetrasvaratā'kṣiromasaṃtulanaṃ nidrā jṛṃbhaṇaṃ mūrcchāchardiraruciḥ pādaśopho'mle'bhilāṣasteṣu coccāvaceṣu bhāveṣviti

hindi: और उसके रज को वहन करने वाले स्रोतसों यानी शरीर की वाहिनियों के मार्ग गर्भ द्वारा रुक जाते हैं।
english: And the paths of her srotas (bodily channels) that carry rajas (menstrual blood) are blocked by the embryo.

text_flags.why: possible: the genitive plural 'rajovāhinīnām' is needed to agree with srotasām; the print lacks 'nā'

notes: 'srotas' (channel) is a doctrinal term, kept with a short plain gloss, not forced to a single modern structure. 'rajovāhinī' = rajas-carrying (channels); rajas = menstrual blood (standard in this context).

hindi: इसलिए उसके बाद आर्तव यानी स्त्री का रज दिखाई नहीं देता।
english: Therefore, from then on, the ārtava (menstrual fluid) is not seen.
notes: Refers to the stopping of the menstrual flow after conception (see line 10 (card 10)). Identification: ārtava = menstrual fluid (standard).

words.gloss: by itself; being built up, increasing
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, pres. pass. part. upa-√ci, n. nom. sg.

hindi: तब वह नीचे रुका हुआ, अन्य, अन्य, अपने आप बढ़ता हुआ, अपरा यानी सम्भवतः आँवल, ऐसा कहते हैं।
english: Then that, checked below—other, other—increasing of itself, they call aparā (probably the afterbirth, placenta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'aparam aparam' may be a repeated word; the duplicate is kept in the translation

notes: Difficult line; the grammar is not secure. 'tat' is taken as the blood/fluid of the previous units (not stated here). The doubled 'aparam' could be a dittography, or mean 'one other thing, another thing'. 'aparā' (f.) is the standard Āyurvedic term for the afterbirth (placenta); the identification is probable, and the translation keeps the Sanskrit word. The reading 'aparā iti' is taken from 'aparetyāhuḥ'. Subject of 'āhuḥ' is unstated ('they').

hindi: जरायु यानी सम्भवतः गर्भ की झिल्ली, ऐसा दूसरे कहते हैं।
english: Others say: jarāyu (probably the foetal membrane).

text_flags.why: certain: a doubled u in the print; jarāyuḥ + iti gives jarāyur iti

notes: The verb 'say' is carried from line 12 (card 12) (āhuḥ) and appears in the translation as 'say' for the plural subject 'others'. GROUPING: appears to continue line 12 (card 12) (an alternative name for the same thing). jarāyu = foetal membrane / afterbirth (probable; the term is also used for membranes enclosing the foetus).

hindi: रक्त के स्थिर हो जाने पर रोमराजी यानी रोमों की पंक्ति प्रकट होती है, और रक्त ऊपर जरायु के शेष को प्राप्त होता है।
english: But when the blood has settled, a line of hair (romarājī) appears, and the blood goes upward to the remainder of the jarāyu.

text_flags.why: spacing: two words run together; certain

notes: Ambiguous: 'jarāyuśeṣam ... asṛk pratipadyate' could also mean 'the remainder of the jarāyu goes up as blood'. The first reading (asṛk subject, jarāyuśeṣam object) is taken. 'romarājī' is a line of hair; whose body it appears on is not stated. 'asṛk' (asṛj) is a synonym of rakta, both 'blood'.
lines_deva: स्थिते तु रक्ते रोमराजी प्रादुर्भवतिजरायुशेषं चोर्ध्वमसृक् प्रतिपद्यते
lines_iast: sthite tu rakte romarājī prādurbhavatijarāyuśeṣaṃ cordhvamasṛk pratipadyate

words.gloss: plump; cheek; breast; state of being
black; lip; nipple; state of being

hindi: उससे मोटे गाल और स्तन होना तथा काले ओंठ और चूचुक होना।
english: From that, plumpness of cheeks and breasts, and blackness of lips and nipples.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is stated and none is supplied. The tokens are printed joined (tasmātpīnakapolapayodharatākṛṣṇauṣṭhacūcukatvaṃ). payodhara (lit. 'milk-bearer') = breast; kapola = cheek; cūcuka = nipple (standard). Whose face and breasts is not stated; the sense is the signs of changes of pregnancy.

words.gloss: of her who has given birth

hindi: स्तनों में ही स्थित, अनुमानित पाठ पर कफ से रंजित, प्रसूता में स्तन्य यानी दूध की अवस्था को प्राप्त, फिर आहार के रस से पुष्ट होता है।
english: That which has its resting place in the breasts, on a conjectural reading tinged by Kapha, having reached the state of breast-milk (stanyatā) in her who has given birth, is nourished again by the rasa of food.

text_flags.why: possible: 'keṃpha' for kapha and an extra 'ta' in 'upataraṃjitaṃ'; the intended word is probably kapha-uparañjita 'tinged with Kapha'; reading uncertain

notes: Subject not stated (probably the blood of line 14 (card 14); not asserted). The reading 'tinged with Kapha' is conjectural (damaged-looking word keṃphopataraṃjitaṃ). 'rasa' here = nutrient fluid of food. Identification: stanya = breast milk (standard).
lines_deva: स्तनाश्रयमेव च केंफोपतरंजितं स्तन्यतामुपगतं प्रसूतायाः पुनराहाररसेनाप्यायते
lines_iast: stanāśrayameva ca keṃphopataraṃjitaṃ stanyatāmupagataṃ prasūtāyāḥ punarāhārarasenāpyāyate

words.gloss: kalala (the first embryonic mass; early embryo, probable)

hindi: उनमें पहले मास में कलल यानी सम्भवतः आरम्भिक भ्रूण उत्पन्न होता है।
english: Of these, in the first month a kalala (the first embryonic mass, probably the early embryo) arises.
notes: kalala is the first stage of the embryo; the modern equivalent (zygote or early embryo) is probable, not exact.

hindi: दूसरे मास में घन, पेशी या अर्बुद, और उनसे क्रम से पुरुष, स्त्री और नपुंसक।
english: In the second month, a dense mass (ghana), or a peśī (muscle-like lump), or an arbuda (lump); from these, in order, males, females and neuters (napuṃsaka).
notes: No verb is stated or supplied. The pairing of ghana, peśī, arbuda with male, female, neuter is left to the order word 'kramāt' ('in order'); the text does not state the pairing and it is not stated as fact here. 'peśyarbudaṃ' = peśī + arbudam.
lines_deva: द्वितीये घनः पेश्यर्बुदं वा तेभ्यः क्रमात्पुंस्त्रीनपुंसकानि
lines_iast: dvitīye ghanaḥ peśyarbudaṃ vā tebhyaḥ kramātpuṃstrīnapuṃsakāni

hindi: तीसरे मास में वह पाँच प्रकार से अंकुरित होता है।
english: In the third month it sprouts in five ways.
notes: Subject 'it' (the embryo) is understood.

hindi: वह जैसे कि।
english: Namely:
notes: Stock formula 'tad yathā', 'namely', introducing the list in line 21 (card 21).

hindi: दोनों सक्थि यानी जाँघें, दोनों बाहु और सिर।
english: The two thighs (legs), the two arms and the head.
notes: The list of the five sprouts of line 19 (card 19) (two legs, two arms, head = five). No verb. sakthi = thigh, also used for the leg.

words.gloss: thigh; beginning with; sprouting; one; time (at the same time as the sprouting of the legs and the rest)

words.gram: dvandva of aṅga, avayava, indriya (sarva qualifies all), n. nom. pl.

words.gloss: birth; after; time; born (born after birth)

hindi: और जाँघों आदि के अंकुरित होने के समय ही सब अंग, अवयव और इन्द्रियाँ एक साथ उत्पन्न होते हैं, जन्म के बाद के समय में उत्पन्न होने वाले दाँत आदि को छोड़कर; किन्तु क्रम से वे स्पष्ट हो जाते हैं।
english: And at the very time of the sprouting of the thighs and the rest, all the limbs, parts and sense organs (indriya) come to be simultaneously, except those born in the time after birth, the teeth and the rest; but in order they become distinct.
notes: 'krameṇa tu spaṣṭībhavanti': the subject 'they' could be all the parts or only the later-born ones; the translation leaves it open. 'sakthyādi' = sakthi + ādi, 'the thighs and the rest' (the five sprouts of 21). 'indriya' = sense organ (standard); kept as indriya. 'sarvāṃgāvayaveṃdriyāṇi' is read as a series of three terms, not a closed compound.
lines_deva: सक्थ्यादिप्ररोहैककालमेव च सर्वांगावयवेंद्रियाणि युगपत्संभवन्त्यन्यत्र जन्मोत्तरकालजेभ्यो दंतादिभ्यः क्रमेण तु स्पष्टीभवंति
lines_iast: sakthyādiprarohaikakālameva ca sarvāṃgāvayaveṃdriyāṇi yugapatsaṃbhavantyanyatra janmottarakālajebhyo daṃtādibhyaḥ krameṇa tu spaṣṭībhavaṃti

hindi: यह प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था है।
english: This is the prakṛti (the natural, normal state).
notes: Copula understood. Here prakṛti means the normal course (as against vikṛti in 24), not the body-type or the primal matter.

hindi: इससे अन्यथा विकृति यानी असामान्य अवस्था है।
english: Otherwise than this is vikṛti (deviation, the abnormal state).
notes: Copula understood. Printed 'vikṛtirato'nyathā' = vikṛtiḥ + ataḥ + anyathā.

words.gloss: male; female; neuter; any one of; sign; conforming to

hindi: और गर्भ के, अपने अपने अनुसार, पुरुष, स्त्री या नपुंसक में से किसी एक के लिंग के अनुरूप ही भाव मन में और शरीर में स्थित होते हैं।
english: And, each according to its own, the states (bhāva) of the embryo that conform exactly to the sign (liṅga) of one of male, female or neuter become established in the mind and in the body.

text_flags.why: possible: 'anyatarma' appears to be anyatama ('any one of the three') with an extra r; the final -ā before eva is correct sandhi for -āḥ and is not an error
possible: visarga normally stays before m of manasi; the print has bhāvā

notes: The reading of 'anyatarma' is uncertain: anyatara 'either of two' or anyatama 'any of many'; for three genders anyatama is expected. 'bhāva' translated 'state'; the text does not specify which states.
lines_deva: यथास्वंच गर्भस्य पुंस्त्रीनपुंसकान्यतर्मलिंगानुरूपा एव भावा मनसि शरीरे च संतिष्ठंते
lines_iast: yathāsvaṃca garbhasya puṃstrīnapuṃsakānyatarmaliṃgānurūpā eva bhāvā manasi śarīre ca saṃtiṣṭhaṃte

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, किन्तु लिंगों के मिश्रण में विशेष निर्धारण वहाँ से होता है जहाँ अधिकता हो; उससे भाव दोनों में से किसी एक के होते हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading: but in a mixture of signs, the distinguishing (determination) is from where there is greater abundance; from that, the states are those of one or the other.

text_flags.why: possible: yava (barley) makes no sense here; 'yato ... tato' is the correlative pair
possible: plural nominative agreeing with bhāvāḥ

notes: Reading uncertain. 'vaiśeṣikaṃ' with spurious anusvāra is taken as the neuter nominative 'distinguishing (determination)'; the other reading, vaiśeṣika as a first member, is possible. The meaning of 'anyatarāḥ' ('of one or the other') is the best fit. Hindi 'होता है' renders a nominal sentence.
lines_deva: वैशेषिकंलिंगसंकरे तु यवो भूयस्त्वं ततोऽन्यतरा भावाः
lines_iast: vaiśeṣikaṃliṃgasaṃkare tu yavo bhūyastvaṃ tato'nyatarā bhāvāḥ

hindi: वह जैसे कि।
english: Namely:
notes: Stock formula 'tad yathā', introducing the list in line 28 (card 28).

hindi: क्लैब्य यानी सम्भवतः नपुंसकता, भीरुता, आत्मविश्वास की कमी, मोह, अस्थिरता, नीचे भारीपन, कसाव की कमी, शिथिलता, मृदुता, गर्भाशय और बीज के भाव, तथा उसी प्रकार अन्य उचित भी, ये स्त्री बनाने वाले भाव हैं।
english: Klaibya (unmanliness), timidity, lack of confidence, bewilderment, unsteadiness, heaviness below, lack of compactness, laxity, softness, the states of the womb and seed, and likewise other fitting (ones): these are the woman-making states.
notes: The list in 28 and the closing 'strīkarā bhāvāḥ' are one sentence: the listed states are 'woman-making states'. 'garbhāśaya-bīja-bhāvāḥ' is taken as 'states of womb and seed' (as in the womb and seed of a woman); the exact sense of the first-member relation is not secure. 'yuktāḥ ... apare' is read 'and other fitting (ones)'; 'yukta' may also mean 'joined, connected'. The print 'strīkarābhāvāḥ' = strīkarāḥ bhāvāḥ. klaibya is not simply impotence; here a character-trait of unmanliness; modern equivalent (impotence/lack of virility) is probable.
lines_deva: क्लैब्यं भीरुत्वमवैशारद्यं मोहोऽनवस्थानमधोगुरुत्वमसंहननं शैथिल्यं मार्दवं गर्भाशयबीजभावास्तथा युक्ताश्चापरे स्त्रीकराभावाः
lines_iast: klaibyaṃ bhīrutvamavaiśāradyaṃ moho'navasthānamadhogurutvamasaṃhananaṃ śaithilyaṃ mārdavaṃ garbhāśayabījabhāvāstathā yuktāścāpare strīkarābhāvāḥ

hindi: इनसे विपरीत पुरुष बनाने वाले हैं।
english: Those opposite to these are the man-making (ones).
notes: 'bhāvāḥ' is understood from 28. The sentence is nominal: copula understood.

hindi: मिले जुले नपुंसक बनाने वाले हैं।
english: The mixed (ones) are the neuter-making (ones).
notes: 'bhāvāḥ' understood from 28; copula understood.

hindi: और तब इसकी चेतना पूर्ण रूप से प्रकट हो जाती है।
english: And then its consciousness (cetanā) becomes fully manifest.

text_flags.why: spacing: words run together (ca + asya + cetanā); certain

notes: 'asya' refers to the embryo.

hindi: और तब से वह हिलता है और पाँचों इन्द्रियों के विषयों में अभिलाषा करता है।
english: And from then on it moves (throbs) and has desire for the five objects of the senses.

text_flags.why: likely: 'iṃdviya' is a letter scramble of indriya (dvi/dri)

notes: 'abhilāṣaṃ karoti' literally 'makes desire'. Subject 'it' (the embryo) understood. 'spandate' may mean 'moves' or 'throbs'.

hindi: क्योंकि इसका हृदय माता से उत्पन्न है और उसके रस को ले जाने वाली धमनियों यानी वाहिनियों द्वारा माता के हृदय से जुड़ा रहता है।
english: For its heart is born of the mother, and is joined to the mother's heart by dhamanīs (vessels) that carry the rasa of that (tad, referent not stated).
notes: 'tad' in 'tadrasa' is not clearly stated: it may mean 'the rasa of that (mother)' or 'of that (the heart)'; 'its rasa' in the translation is a literal placeholder for that. dhamanī = vessel (tube-like channel); whether it means artery or umbilical vessel is not stated and is not asserted. The printed token runs words together (tadrasahāriṇībhirdhamanībhirmātṛhṛdayenābhisaṃbaddhaṃ). hṛdaya = heart (standard).

hindi: इसलिए उन दोनों में उनके द्वारा श्रद्धा यानी इच्छा उत्पन्न होती है।
english: Therefore, in the two, through those (vessels), a longing (śraddhā) arises.
notes: 'tayoḥ' is taken as 'in the two (the mother and the embryo)' and 'tābhiḥ' as the dhamanīs of 33; both are the natural reading but are not stated. śraddhā here: longing, desire (see the daurhṛda lines 35-38 (card 35/37)), not 'faith'. GROUPING: appears to continue 33. Alternative: 'tayoḥ' may refer to the two hearts (the mother's and the embryo's, line 33 (card 33)), which fits dvihṛdayā in line 35 (card 35); not asserted.

hindi: और इसी प्रकार दो हृदय वाली स्त्री को दौर्हृदिनी यानी इच्छाओं वाली कहते हैं।
english: And so they call a woman with two hearts (dvihṛdayā) daurhṛdinī (a woman with longings).

text_flags.why: possible: hṛ printed as ha; daurhṛdinī from daurhṛda 'longing' is expected

notes: 'dvihṛdayā' = literally 'two-hearted'; used of a pregnant woman. 'daurhṛda' (longing of a pregnant woman) is the standard term. Whether the 'two hearts' refers to the mother's heart and the embryo's heart is not stated here.

hindi: दूसरे लोग तीन पक्ष से लेकर पाँचवें मास तक दौर्हृद का काल बताते हैं। और इच्छा तीव्र होने पर इसे कामनानुसार अहित भी, हित से युक्त करके, देना चाहिए।
english: Others, however, give the time of the daurhṛda (longing) as from three fortnights up to the fifth month. And when the wish is intense, one should give her, as desired, even the unwholesome, joined with the wholesome.

text_flags.why: possible: 'daurhada' for daurhṛda (hṛ printed as ha)
spacing: words run together; certain

notes: [02.02.36] 'ā pañcamāt māsāt' = up to the fifth month; whether the fifth month is included is not clear. Three fortnights is one and a half months. [02.02.37] 'hitopasaṃhitam' is read as 'joined with the wholesome'; the text does not say what is joined. No nouns are supplied (the objects are neuter adjectives). The subject of 'dadyāt' is unstated ('one').

words.gram: pres. part. anu-√car, m. nom. sg.

hindi: क्योंकि दौर्हृद की उपेक्षा से कुपित वायु शरीर के भीतर घूमता हुआ गर्भ का नाश, यानी सम्भवतः गर्भपात, या विरूपता कर सकता है।
english: For, from disregard of the daurhṛda (longing), vāyu (Vāta), agitated and moving about inside the body, may cause destruction (probably miscarriage) or deformity of the embryo.

text_flags.why: likely: spurious ṃ before the avagraha

notes: 'vināśa' (destruction of the embryo) is the loss of the pregnancy, i.e. probably miscarriage; the translation keeps 'destruction'. 'vimāna' = disregard, dishonouring (of the wish). The print 'daurhṛdavimānāddhi' = daurhṛda-vimānāt + hi. 'kuryāt' read as optative 'may cause'.
lines_deva: दौर्हृदविमानाद्धि वायुःप्रकुपितोंऽतःशरीरमनुचरन् गर्भस्य विनाशं वैरूप्यं वा कुर्यात्
lines_iast: daurhṛdavimānāddhi vāyuḥprakupitoṃ'taḥśarīramanucaran garbhasya vināśaṃ vairūpyaṃ vā kuryāt

words.gloss: one whose longing (daurhṛda) has been obtained
division into limbs and minor limbs

hindi: जिस स्त्री की दौर्हृद यानी गर्भावस्था की इच्छा पूरी कर दी गई हो, वह वीर्यवान् यानी शक्तिशाली और दीर्घ आयु वाले पुत्र को जन्म देती है। चौथे में, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अङ्ग और प्रत्यङ्ग का विभाग प्रकट हो जाता है और गर्भ स्थिर हो जाता है।
english: But she whose longing (daurhṛda, the longing of pregnancy) has been fulfilled bears a vigorous and long-lived son. In the fourth, on a conjectural reading, the division into limbs and minor limbs is manifest, and the embryo (garbha) becomes stable.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mattyaṃga' is not a word; 'pratyaṅga' (minor limb) fits the sense and the same list in line 60 (card 58) (aṅga-pratyaṅga); tya/tty and pra/ma confusion is common in this print
possible: 'pranyakta' is not a word; 'pravyakta' (manifest) fits; vy/ny confusion

notes: [02.02.39] GROUPING: this unit appears to continue a discussion of daurhṛda begun in the preceding unit (outside this chunk). The subject is the feminine participle only; no noun 'woman' is printed. daurhṛda = the longing of a pregnant woman (standard). [02.02.40] 'caturthe' = in the fourth; the noun (month) is not printed and is understood from the sequence of lines 39-43 (card 38/41); it is left out of the translation. 'bhavati' serves both clauses (is manifest / becomes stable). Both text_flags are conjectural, so the reading is not firm.
lines_deva: लब्धदौर्हृदा तु वीर्यवंतं चिरायुषं च पुत्रं प्रसूते
lines_iast: labdhadaurhṛdā tu vīryavaṃtaṃ cirāyuṣaṃ ca putraṃ prasūte

hindi: पाँचवें में मन अधिक जागृत हो जाता है और मांस तथा रक्त की वृद्धि होती है।
english: In the fifth, the mind (manas) becomes more awakened, and there is an increase of flesh (māṃsa) and blood (śoṇita).
notes: The noun (month) after 'pañcame' is not printed; understood from the sequence. 'bhavati' is carried over to the second clause ('there is'). śoṇita = blood (standard).

words.gloss: hair, body-hair, nails, bones (asthi), sinews (snāyu; probably tendons/ligaments), and so on

hindi: छठे में केश, रोम, नख, अस्थि, स्नायु आदि प्रकट हो जाते हैं और बल तथा रंग की वृद्धि होती है।
english: In the sixth, hair, body-hair, nails, bones (asthi), sinews (snāyu) and so on become manifest, and there is an increase of strength and complexion (varṇa).
notes: The token is split once as one dvandva followed by ādīni and abhivyaktāni; the printed 'snāyavādīni' is snāyu + ādīni with the u written as av before a vowel. snāyu: sinew, probably tendon or ligament (probable; the word covers several fibrous structures). varṇa here = colour of the skin, complexion. 'there is' is the carried-over verb of the first clause.

hindi: सातवें में सब अंगों की पूर्णता।
english: In the seventh, completeness of all the limbs.
notes: Nominal line with no verb; none supplied in the translation. The noun (month) after 'saptame' is understood from the sequence.

hindi: आठवें में गर्भ माता से और माता गर्भ से, रस यानी पोषक द्रव को ले जाने वाली वाहिनियों के द्वारा, बार-बार एक-दूसरे से ओज यानी जीवन-सार ग्रहण करते हैं।
english: In the eighth, the embryo (garbha) from the mother and the mother from the embryo, by the channels (vāhinī) that carry rasa (nutrient fluid), repeatedly take ojas (vital essence) from each other.

text_flags.why: possible: stray anusvāra; the ablative suffix -tas before the voiced g of 'garbhataḥ' gives 'mātṛto'

notes: ojas = the vital essence (ojas); no modern equivalent is forced. rasa here = the nutrient fluid (rasa dhātu). The verb is dual, with subjects garbha and mātā. 'aṣṭamegarbhaśca' is printed as one token (aṣṭame + garbhaḥ + ca).

hindi: इसलिए उस समय गर्भवती स्त्री कभी प्रसन्न होती है और कभी म्लान यानी मुरझाई हुई, और वैसे ही गर्भ भी।
english: Therefore at that time the pregnant woman is at one moment glad and at another languid, and likewise the embryo (garbha).
notes: 'bhavatimuhur' is printed without a space (bhavati + muhuḥ); only the word division, no spelling error. The verb is carried over to 'tathā garbhaḥ' (elliptical); no verb is supplied in the translation beyond the repeated 'is'. mlānā = faded, languid.
lines_deva: तस्मात्तदा गर्भिणी मुहुर्मुदिता भवतिमुहुर्म्लाना तथा गर्भः
lines_iast: tasmāttadā garbhiṇī muhurmuditā bhavatimuhurmlānā tathā garbhaḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार तब गर्भ का जन्म विपत्ति से युक्त होता है।
english: Thus the birth of the embryo (garbha) is then accompanied by calamity (vyāpatti).
notes: 'vyāpatti' = calamity, ruin, misfortune; it is a neuter agreeing with 'janma'. 'then' refers to the eighth month of line 44 (card 42); the text does not name it here.

hindi: ओज के अस्थिर होने के कारण।
english: Because of the unsteadiness of ojas (the vital essence).
notes: Dependent ablative phrase which appears to give the reason for line 46 (card 44); a single token with the avagraha 'ojaso'navasthitatvāt'. ojas = vital essence (no modern equivalent forced).

words.gloss: directed toward coming out, on the point of coming out

words.gram: pres. part. anu-√bhū, m. nom. sg.

hindi: क्योंकि इस निकलने के लिए उन्मुख के, पलटने आदि का अनुभव करते हुए, यह ओज से वियोग है।
english: For thus, in this one who is on the point of coming out, experiencing turning round and the like, this is the separation from ojas (the vital essence).
notes: Hard line; read with confidence only in outline. 'niṣkramaṇonmukhasyaparivartanādīnyanubhavan' is printed without a space between unmukhasya and parivartana. Syntax is loose: asya ... unmukhasya is genitive while 'anubhavan' is nominative, while 'ojasā' (instrumental) with 'viyoga' is acceptable (viyoga and viyukta take the instrumental); the translation follows the printed forms. 'is' is a copula understood. 'eṣaḥ' (printed as eṣa + ojasā = eṣaujasā) is taken as 'this'.

words.gloss: made by the continuation of the impression (saṃskāra) of ojas

hindi: और यदि इसका कुछ समय तक साँस लेना हो भी, तो वह कटे हुए अंग की तरह, ओज के संस्कार यानी छाप के बने रहने से किया हुआ है।
english: And even if there may be breathing of this one for some time, that is made by the continuation of the impression (saṃskāra) of ojas, like that of a severed limb.
notes: Continues the argument of 47-48. The comparison 'like a severed limb' is attached to the whole phrase 'that is made by the continuation of the ojas impression'; it could also be read as 'as in a severed limb'. 'tacchinnasya' is tat + chinnasya. saṃskāra = lingering impression or impetus.

words.gloss: of the mother, in the mother
because of the stability of ojas

hindi: परन्तु माता में ओज के स्थिर होने के कारण, रस का एक अंश में संक्रान्त हो जाने पर केवल ग्लानि ही।
english: But in the mother, because of the stability of her ojas, when rasa (nutrient fluid) has passed over in one part, there is only weariness (glāni).
notes: Locative absolute 'rase saṃkrānte'. 'there is' is a copula understood; the Hindi supplies none. The closing 'iti' ends the view stated in 48-50; the next unit begins 'Others, however, say'. 'ekadeśena' = in one part, partially.

hindi: दूसरे लोग फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, however, say.
notes: Introduces the alternative view that follows in 52. The statement of the view is not complete in this unit.

words.gloss: because of being the share of Nairṛta (belonging to Nirṛti)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर नैर्ऋत यानी निर्ऋति से सम्बन्धित भाग होने के कारण वहाँ गर्भ की मृत्यु।
english: Because, on a conjectural reading, it is the Nairṛta share (the share belonging to Nirṛti), there, death of the embryo (garbha).

text_flags.why: possible: 'bhāgatavāt' is not a form; 'bhāgatvāt' (because of being the share) fits the sense; extra 'a'

notes: Nominal; no verb in the translation. Nairṛta = belonging to Nirṛti, the deity of ruin and death (probable; the word can also mean the south-west quarter). What the 'share' is (probably the period named in the preceding discussion) is not stated; 'tatra' is read as 'there, in that case'. Meaning not firm.

words.gloss: intent on worship of the deities

hindi: इसलिए प्रसव को रोकने के लिए स्त्री स्नान किए हुए, शुद्ध, ब्रह्मचारिणी यानी ब्रह्मचर्य का पालन करने वाली और देवताओं की आराधना में तत्पर हो।
english: Therefore, in order to prevent delivery (prasava), the woman should be bathed, pure, chaste (brahmacāriṇī, observing brahmacarya) and intent on the worship of the deities.
notes: 'śucirbrahmacāriṇī' is śuciḥ + brahmacāriṇī; śucir is a separate adjective, not a compound member. brahmacāriṇī = one who keeps brahmacarya, here best taken as chaste.
lines_deva: तस्मात्प्रसवप्रतिषेधार्थं स्त्री स्नाता शुचिर्ब्रह्मचारिणी दैवताराधनपरमा स्यात्
lines_iast: tasmātprasavapratiṣedhārthaṃ strī snātā śucirbrahmacāriṇī daivatārādhanaparamā syāt

words.gloss: an offering (bali) of meat and boiled rice

hindi: और यहाँ मांस और ओदन यानी पके चावल की बलि यानी भेंट अर्पित करे।
english: And here one should offer a bali (offering) of meat (māṃsa) and boiled rice (odana).
notes: Subject of 'nirvapet' not printed ('one'). 'here' = in this case, as in 53. odana = boiled rice (standard).

hindi: उसमें एक दिन बीत जाने पर भी वे प्रसव का समय एक वर्ष तक कहते हैं।
english: Even when one day has passed in that (period), they speak of a time of delivery up to a year.
notes: What 'tasmin' refers to is not clear from the unit: probably the stage or period discussed in 52-54. 'ā-saṃvatsarāt' = up to a year (ā with the ablative). Rendered literally; sense not firm.

hindi: इसके बाद वह विकारी यानी विकार वाला हो जाता है।
english: After this, (he) becomes disordered (vikārin, subject to disorder).
notes: The subject is not printed; probably the child, but the text does not say. 'vikārī' is masculine. The sense of 'disorder' is not specified.

hindi: गर्भ माता की पीठ की ओर मुख किए हुए, ललाट पर अञ्जलि बाँधे हुए और अंगों को सिकोड़े हुए, गर्भ-कोष्ठ यानी सम्भवतः गर्भाशय की गुहा में दाहिने पार्श्व का आश्रय लेकर पुमान् यानी पुरुष टिकता है, बाएँ का आश्रय लेकर स्त्री और मध्य का आश्रय लेकर नपुंसक।
english: The embryo (garbha), facing the mother's back, with the palms joined (añjali) at the forehead and the limbs contracted, stays in the garbha-koṣṭha (probably the uterine cavity), the male (pumān) resting on the right side, the female (strī) on the left, the neuter (napuṃsaka) in the middle.
notes: Elliptical: 'āśritya avatiṣṭhate' is carried over to 'vāmaṃ strī' and 'madhyaṃ napuṃsakaṃ'; the glosses 'resting on' are understood. garbha-koṣṭha = the cavity in which the embryo lies, the uterus (probable). napuṃsaka = neither male nor female (the neuter); the word is used of a person. Rendered exactly as printed.
lines_deva: गर्भस्तु मातुः पृष्ठाभिमुखो ललाटे कृतांजलिः संकुचितांगो गर्भकोष्ठे दक्षिणपार्श्वमाश्रित्यावतिष्ठते पुमान् वामं स्त्री मध्यं नपुंसकं
lines_iast: garbhastu mātuḥ pṛṣṭhābhimukho lalāṭe kṛtāṃjaliḥ saṃkucitāṃgo garbhakoṣṭhe dakṣiṇapārśvamāśrityāvatiṣṭhate pumān vāmaṃ strī madhyaṃ napuṃsakaṃ

hindi: और वहाँ स्थित गर्भ, माता के सोने पर सोता है और माता के जागने पर जाग जाता है।
english: And staying there, the embryo (garbha) sleeps when the mother is sleeping and wakes when she is awake.

text_flags.why: possible: 'svāpiti' is not a normal present of √svap (the causative is svāpayati); 'svapiti' fits the sense and the matching 'svapantyām'

notes: 'garbhomātari' is printed as one token without a space (garbho mātari). Locative absolutes 'mātari svapantyām' and 'prabuddhāyām' (mātari carried over).
lines_deva: तत्र स्थितश्च गर्भोमातरि स्वपंत्यां स्वापिति प्रबुद्धायां प्रबुध्यते
lines_iast: tatra sthitaśca garbhomātari svapaṃtyāṃ svāpiti prabuddhāyāṃ prabudhyate

words.gloss: because of dependent functioning (lit. functioning under another's control)

hindi: और गर्भ की दूसरे के अधीन वृत्ति के कारण।
english: And because of the dependent functioning (paratantra-vṛtti) of the embryo (garbha).
notes: Nominal fragment; vṛtteḥ is taken as an ablative of reason, though the genitive form is identical, so it could also read 'of the dependent functioning'. paratantra = under another's control. Probably gives the reason for the statements in 58; the unit has no verb of its own.

words.gloss: from impregnation (niṣeka; the infusion of semen, standard)
the moistening (upasneha) and the sweating/warming (upasveda) of the womb (garbhāśaya, the uterus; standard)
words.gram: m. nom. du. (dvandva, in tat-puruṣa with garbhāśaya)

words.gloss: of one whose limbs and minor limbs are becoming manifest
duct, tube (nāḍī; probably the umbilical cord)

hindi: निषेक यानी गर्भाधान से लेकर गर्भाशय का उपस्नेह यानी भीगना और उपस्वेद यानी पसीना पोषण का साधन है। उसके बाद, अनुमानित पाठ पर, जिसके अंग-प्रत्यंग प्रकट हो रहे हैं उस इसकी नाभि में नाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः गर्भनाल बँधी है; नाड़ी में, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अपरा यानी जेर; उसमें माता का हृदय।
english: From niṣeka (impregnation) onward, the moistening (upasneha) and sweating or warming (upasveda) of the womb (garbhāśaya) are the means of sustenance (vartana). Then, in this one whose limbs and minor limbs are becoming manifest (on a conjectural reading), a duct (nāḍī, probably the umbilical cord) is fastened at the navel; in the duct, the aparā (placenta; on a conjectural reading); in that, the mother's heart (hṛdaya).

text_flags.why: possible: 'parā' alone does not fit; line 61 (card 59) has 'aparām' (the placenta) as the next link, so the 'a' of 'aparā' appears to have dropped
possible: stray 'ma' before 'pratyaṅga'; compare the same list in 40; the avagraha mark in 'syā'sya' is spurious (a + a = ā)

notes: Elliptical: 'pratibaddhā' is carried over to 'aparā' and to 'mātṛhṛdayam' (the connections are 'fastened'), and no verb is supplied beyond the first. 'garbhāśayopasnehopasvedau' is taken as upasneha and upasveda of the garbhāśaya; the other possible reading (garbhāśaya as a third item in the dvandva) is less likely. niṣeka = emission or infusion of semen, so impregnation (standard). nāḍī = the umbilical cord (probable); aparā = placenta (standard). Both text_flags are conjectures.
lines_deva: निषेकात्प्रभृति गर्भाशयोपस्नेहोपस्वेदौ वर्तनं ततो व्यक्तीभवदंगमप्रत्यंगस्याऽस्य नाभ्यां प्रतिबद्धा नाडी नाड्यांपरा तस्यां मातृहृदयं
lines_iast: niṣekātprabhṛti garbhāśayopasnehopasvedau vartanaṃ tato vyaktībhavadaṃgamapratyaṃgasyā'sya nābhyāṃ pratibaddhā nāḍī nāḍyāṃparā tasyāṃ mātṛhṛdayaṃ

words.gloss: through the vessels (dhamanī; probably blood vessels)

words.gram: pres. part. ā. √spand, m. nom. sg.

hindi: तब माता के हृदय से आहार-रस धमनी यानी वाहिकाओं के द्वारा स्पन्दित होता हुआ अपरा यानी जेर को प्राप्त होता है।
english: Then from the mother's heart the rasa of food (āhāra-rasa), pulsating through the vessels (dhamanī), reaches the aparā (placenta).
notes: dhamanī = vessel, here probably blood vessels (probable; the word is used for arteries and other channels). spandamāna = throbbing, pulsating.

hindi: तब क्रम से नाभि को।
english: Then, in sequence, to the navel.
notes: GROUPING: this fragment appears to continue the movement described in 61 (upaiti, 'reaches') and to lead into 63; no verb is printed and none is supplied. Kept as its own unit as in the edition.

words.gloss: in the pakvāśaya (the site of digested matter, probably the large intestine)
by its own bodily fire (kāyāgni, digestive fire)

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √pac, m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: from the abundance of the clear part (prasāda)
nourishing the dhātus and the rest

hindi: और तब वह फिर गर्भ के पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत में, अपनी कायाग्नि यानी शरीर की पाचन-अग्नि से पकाया जाता हुआ, प्रसाद यानी निर्मल भाग की अधिकता से धातु आदि की पुष्टि करने वाला हो जाता है।
english: And then it again, in the embryo's pakvāśaya (the site of digested matter, probably the large intestine), being cooked by its own bodily fire (kāyāgni), becomes, through the abundance of the clear part (prasāda), nourishing to the dhātus and the rest.
notes: 'sa' refers to the rasa of food of 61. kāyāgni = the digestive fire of the body (standard). pakvāśaya = the receptacle of digested matter; the large intestine is the usual equivalent (probable). prasāda = the clear, pure part of what is digested. 'punar' read as 'then, in turn'. dhātu is kept untranslated as a doctrinal term.
lines_deva: ततश्च स पुनर्गर्भस्य पक्वाशये स्वकायाग्निना पच्यमानः प्रसादबाहुल्याद्धात्वादिपुष्टिकरः संपद्यते
lines_iast: tataśca sa punargarbhasya pakvāśaye svakāyāgninā pacyamānaḥ prasādabāhulyāddhātvādipuṣṭikaraḥ saṃpadyate

hindi: वैसे ही रोमकूपों से उपस्नेह यानी भीगना, और रस ही पयस् यानी दूध या जल बना हुआ।
english: Likewise, through the hair-pores there is moistening (upasneha), and the rasa itself having become payas (milk or water).
notes: Elliptical; 'there is' is a copula understood. payas can mean milk or water; the line does not say which, so both are given. The second half is not a full sentence; the sense of 'rasa itself having become payas' is not firm.

words.gloss: because of the non-entry of food and drink

hindi: जन्म न लिए हुए गर्भ के लिए, अन्न और पान का साक्षात् प्रवेश न होने से और रस के अमल यानी मल से रहित होने से, स्थूल मल का उत्पन्न न होना।
english: In the embryo (garbha) not yet born, because food and drink do not enter directly and because the rasa is free from mala (waste; amala), there is no arising of gross waste (sthūla-mala).
notes: 'ajātasya' and 'garbhasya' are both genitive; 'rasasya' also, so the line can be read as 'of the rasa of the unborn embryo' or as given. 'there is' is a copula understood. The text says gross waste does not arise; it does not say whether fine waste does.

words.gloss: through contact with the prasūti-māruta (the māruta, i.e. Vāta, of parturition)

hindi: परन्तु जन्म के समय प्रसूति-मारुत यानी प्रसव की वायु, सम्भवतः प्रसव-संकुचन, के संयोग से, पलटकर, सिर नीचे किए हुए वह निकलता है; और उसके बाद अपरा यानी जेर, माता के हृदय से अलग होकर।
english: But at the time of birth, through contact with the prasūti-māruta (the māruta, i.e. Vāta, of parturition; probably the contractions of labour), having turned round, he comes out head downward; and afterwards the aparā (placenta), detached from the mother's heart.
notes: The verb 'niṣkrāmati' is carried over to 'aparā' ('comes out'), so the second clause is elliptical and no verb is supplied. 'he' is the unstated subject (the embryo, now born). The 'prasūti-māruta' is the māruta (Vāta) of delivery; its modern equivalent is probably the contractions of labour (probable; not stated in the text). 'parivṛttyā'vākśirā' is parivṛttyā + avākśirāḥ.

hindi: यह प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था है।
english: This is the natural state (prakṛti).
notes: Copula understood. prakṛti here = the natural, normal state of things (as opposed to vikṛti in 68), not the doctrinal prakṛti of body constitution.

hindi: इससे अन्यथा विकृति यानी असामान्य अवस्था है।
english: Otherwise than this is abnormality (vikṛti).
notes: Copula understood. 'ato'nyathā' = 'otherwise than this'; the whole line is the counterpart of 67.

words.gloss: with the belly (kukṣi) very raised, and a round embryo (garbha)
delighting in longings (daurhṛda) for seeing, touching and asking about male-named (ones)
with a clear (serene) complexion of the face
with keen hunger and an upward line of body-hair

hindi: वहाँ जो स्त्री पहले दाहिना पैर आगे बढ़ाती है, जिसकी दाहिनी भुजा बलवान् होती है और वह उसी से चेष्टा करती है, जिसके स्तन में पहले दूध दिखाई देता है, अनुमानित पाठ पर जिसकी कुक्षि बहुत ऊँची है और गर्भ गोल है, जो पुरुष नाम वालों को देखने, छूने और उनके विषय में पूछने की दौर्हृद यानी गर्भावस्था की इच्छाओं में रत रहती है, पुरुष नाम वाले स्वप्न देखती है, जिसके मुख का वर्ण प्रसन्न है, जिसकी भूख तीव्र है और रोमों की पंक्ति ऊपर की ओर है, और जो पुरुषों की अभिलाषा करती है, वह पुत्र को जन्म देती है; उसके विपर्यय में कन्या को और मिश्रण में नपुंसक को।
english: There, she who puts the right foot forward first, whose right arm is strong and who acts with it, in whose breast milk is seen first, whose belly (kukṣi) is very raised and the embryo (garbha) round (on a conjectural reading of this compound), who delights in longings (daurhṛda) for seeing, touching and asking about male-named (ones), who sees dreams bearing male names, with a clear complexion of the face, keen hunger, an upward line of body-hair, and who desires men, she bears a son; in the opposite case, a girl; and in a mixture, a napuṃsaka (neuter).

text_flags.why: possible: an extra 'ta' (perhaps a truncated 'tasyāḥ' or a stray syllable); 'ceṣṭate stane ca' makes the sense

notes: Long list of signs ending in 'sā putraṃ prasūte'; 'prasūte' is carried over to 'kanyām' and 'napuṃsakam' (elliptical, no verb supplied). 'putraṃprasūte' is printed without a space. 'prāk' = first, earlier; whether it means in the right breast is not stated. The compound 'atyunnatatatkukṣiparimaṇḍalagarbhā' is uncertain: 'tat' is read as 'her' (tat-kukṣi, her belly) but may be a stray syllable; the reading 'belly very raised, embryo round' is conjectural. 'puruṣānabhilāṣiṇī' is read as puruṣān + abhilāṣiṇī 'desiring men'; the other reading, puruṣa + an-abhilāṣiṇī 'not desiring men', is possible by sandhi. 'napuṃsakaṃ' (acc.) is the object of the carried-over 'prasūte'. 'daurhṛda' = the longing of pregnancy (standard).
lines_deva: तत्र या दक्षिणं पादं पूर्वमभिहरति दक्षिणश्च यस्या बाहुर्बलवांस्तेन च चेष्टतेतस्तने च प्राक् पयो दृश्यतेऽत्युन्नततत्कुक्षिपरिमंडलगर्भा पुन्नामदर्शनस्पर्शनप्रश्नदौर्हृदाभिरता पुन्नामधेयांश्च स्वप्नान् पश्यति प्रसन्नमुखवर्णा तीक्ष्णक्षुदूर्ध्वरोमराजिः पुरुषानभिलाषिणी च सा पुत्रंप्रसूते तद्विपर्यये कन्यां संकरे च नपुंसकं
lines_iast: tatra yā dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ pūrvamabhiharati dakṣiṇaśca yasyā bāhurbalavāṃstena ca ceṣṭatetastane ca prāk payo dṛśyate'tyunnatatatkukṣiparimaṃḍalagarbhā punnāmadarśanasparśanapraśnadaurhṛdābhiratā punnāmadheyāṃśca svapnān paśyati prasannamukhavarṇā tīkṣṇakṣudūrdhvaromarājiḥ puruṣānabhilāṣiṇī ca sā putraṃprasūte tadviparyaye kanyāṃ saṃkare ca napuṃsakaṃ

words.gloss: at the time of the question

hindi: प्रश्न के समय स्त्री जिस लिंग वाले अंग या बाहरी द्रव्य को छूती है, इसके गर्भ को उसी लिंग वाला बताए।
english: At the time of the question, whichever limb or external substance having a gender (liṅga) the woman touches, one should declare her embryo (garbha) to have that same gender.

text_flags.why: possible: 'yad-liṅgam' needs assimilation to 'yal-liṅgam'; the matching 'talliṃgam' later in the unit has ll; dd and ll are confusable in this print

notes: liṅga = the gender or sex-mark of the thing touched (male, female or neuter); the text does not say how it is judged. The subject of 'ādiśet' is unstated ('one'). 'praśnakāle' = at the time of questioning (the question put about the embryo, as the topic suggests).
lines_deva: प्रश्नकाले नारी यद्दिंगमंगं बाह्यद्रव्यं वा परामृशति तल्लिंगमस्या गर्भमादिशेत्
lines_iast: praśnakāle nārī yaddiṃgamaṃgaṃ bāhyadravyaṃ vā parāmṛśati talliṃgamasyā garbhamādiśet

hindi: परन्तु जब मार्ग से भटका हुआ वात गर्भ के रस को ले जाने वाले स्रोतों यानी वाहक मार्गों को सुखा देता है, तब वह वातरोगी और हीन उत्पन्न होता है।
english: But when Vāta, gone astray, dries up the channels (srotas) of the embryo (garbha) that carry rasa, then he is born suffering from a Vāta disease and deficient.

text_flags.why: possible: neuter plural agreeing with 'srotāṃsi' ends in short -i; the printed long -ī may be a slip

notes: 'hīna' = deficient, lacking (in what is not said). 'vātarogī' = suffering from a Vāta disease; the text names no specific illness. The subject of 'jāyate' is the embryo, now born (unstated).
lines_deva: यदातून्मार्गगो वातो गर्भस्य रसवाहिनी स्रोतांसि शोषयति तदा वातरोगी हीनो जायते
lines_iast: yadātūnmārgago vāto garbhasya rasavāhinī srotāṃsi śoṣayati tadā vātarogī hīno jāyate

hindi: या बहुत वर्षों तक पेट में रहता है।
english: Or he stays in the belly (udara) for many years.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 71 as a further outcome after 'tadā' (the subject, the embryo, is not printed). udara = belly, not the disease; the text does not name an illness.

hindi: जब स्त्री और पुरुष दोनों का अर्थ यानी प्रयोजन समान रूप से सिद्ध होता है।
english: When the purpose (artha) is accomplished equally for woman and man.
notes: The dual form 'strīpuṃsayoḥ' can be genitive or locative ('of / in the woman and man'). What the 'purpose' is is not stated in the unit; 74 follows. The sentence is unfinished here: its result is not in this unit.

hindi: या उन दोनों का बीज समान अंश वाला और आमने-सामने होता है।
english: Or the seed (bīja) of the two, of equal portion and face to face.
notes: Elliptical; copula understood. bīja = seed, the generative matter of each parent (probably semen and the female element; no exact modern equivalent is forced). GROUPING: 73 and 74 appear to be conditions of one statement whose result is not in this chunk; the unit as printed contains none.
lines_deva: बीजं वा तयोः समांशं संमुखं च
lines_iast: bījaṃ vā tayoḥ samāṃśaṃ saṃmukhaṃ ca

hindi: और जब बीज किसी भाग में दूषित होता है, तब दो प्रकृति वाला, दो रेतस् यानी वीर्य वाला नपुंसक होता है।
english: And when the seed (bīja) becomes vitiated in a part, then a napuṃsaka (neuter) comes to be, having two natures (dvi-prakṛti) and two seeds (dvi-retas).
notes: 'dvi-prakṛti' = of two natures (here the male and female nature, as the context suggests; not stated). retas = semen (standard), here 'seed'. prakṛti is used in its plain sense of 'nature', not as the constitution term. The two adjectives qualify napuṃsaka.

words.gloss: mṛṇāsuliṅgā (a name; printed form kept, meaning unclear)

hindi: इसी प्रकार पुरुष के विषय में भी, जब शुक्र नामक बीज में बीज दूषित होता है, इत्यादि जोड़ लेना चाहिए: बन्ध्य, बिगड़ी हुई सन्तान वाला, तथा पुरुष की आकृति की प्रधानता वाला, अपुरुष, जिसका नाम मृणासुलिंगा है, उसे उत्पन्न करता है। इसके द्वारा, माता से और पिता से उत्पन्न अवयवों की विकृति के व्याख्यान से, सात्म्य से, रस से और सत्त्व से उत्पन्न अवयवों की विकृति भी समझा दी गई होती है।
english: In just the same way, for a man: 'when, in the seed called śukra, the seed is vitiated' and so on, one should apply it: a barren (one), one of spoiled offspring; and likewise (one) mostly of male shape, a non-male, named mṛṇāsuliṅgā, it produces. By this explanation of the deformity of the mother-born and father-born parts, the deformity of the parts born of sātmya (what suits), of rasa and of sattva (mind) is explained too.

text_flags.why: possible: 'śukarāra-' is not a word; 'śukra-ākhye' (called semen) fits the sense and the pattern of 'śoṇitākhye' in 91; the ra-insertion also appears there

notes: The first part is a quotation ('when ... iti') of the pattern of 91, applied to the man. 'mṛṇāsuliṅgā' is a name after 'nāma'; its meaning is unclear and the print may be corrupt, so it is left untranslated. Several tokens are printed without spaces (bījaṃpraduṣyatītyādiyojayedvaṃdhyaṃ, puruṣākṛtiprāyamapuruṣaṃmṛṇāsuliṃgā, cāvayavānāṃvikṛtivyākhyānena). 'vandhyam' is read as an accusative object (a barren male), 'pūtiprajam' as 'of spoiled offspring' (conjectural). sātmya = what suits one, habit; rasa here is nutritive fluid (probable); sattva = mind (standard); each tagged as the standard reading. Subject of 'janayati' not stated. 'ity-etena' closes the quotation and starts 'by this'.
lines_deva: एवमेव पुंसो यदा शुकरारख्ये बीजे बीजंप्रदुष्यतीत्यादियोजयेद्वंध्यं पूतिप्रजं तथा पुरुषाकृतिप्रायमपुरुषंमृणासुलिंगा नाम जनयतीत्येतेन मातृजानां पितृजानां चावयवानांविकृतिव्याख्यानेन सात्म्यजानां रसजानां सत्त्वजानां चावयवानां विकृतिर्व्याख्याता भवति

hindi: जिस अंग-अवयव के बीज में या बीजांश में उत्पत्ति होती है, उस-उस अंग-अवयव की विकृति उत्पन्न होती है।
english: Of whichever limb-part (aṅga-avayava), in its seed or seed-portion, an origin occurs, of that very limb-part a deformity arises.

english: And when (she) who has obtained a pregnancy resorts, indeed, to Vāta-increasing (ones), the printed 'anakṣam' being unclear (conjecturally 'constantly'), then her provoked Vāyu, moving along the body and lodging in the uterus (garbhāśaya), produces in the embryo the states of being dull (jaḍa), deaf (badhira), mute (mūka), nasal-voiced (minmiṇa), stammering (gadgada), lame (khañja), hunchbacked (kubja), dwarfish (vāmana), deficient in limbs and excessive in limbs, or another Vāta disorder (vātavikāra).

text_flags.why: possible and not firm: 'anakṣam' is not a word in this sense; 'aniśam' (constantly) is a guess from similar letters (śa/kṣa)

notes: The word 'anakṣam' is doubtful; the conjecture 'aniśam, constantly' is not built into the Sanskrit and is only marked in the translation. 'labdhagarbhā' = having obtained an embryo (pregnant). 'garbhasya' goes with the long compound ('in the embryo ... states of ...'); the suffix -tva applies to the whole list. 'minmiṇa' (nasal or indistinct speech) is probable. 'hīnāṅga' (deficient in limbs) and 'adhikāṅga' (excessive in limbs) are as printed. Vāyu is Vāta (standard).

hindi: दृष्टि के भाग को न पहुँचा हुआ तेज जन्मजात अन्धापन है। वही वात से अनुगत विकृत, रूखी, अरुण आँख वाला; पित्त से अनुगत पिंगल आँख वाला; कफ से अनुगत सफ़ेद आँख वाला; रक्त से अनुगत लाल आँख वाला।
english: Light (tejas) that has not reached the share of sight (dṛṣṭibhāga) is congenital blindness (jātyandhatva). That same, followed by Vāta, has deformed, dry, reddish eyes; followed by Pitta, tawny eyes; followed by Kapha, white eyes; followed by blood (rakta), red eyes.

english: For the pregnant woman (garbhiṇī) has the same welfare (yogakṣema) as the embryo.
notes: 'yogakṣema' (attainment and preservation) is read as 'welfare'; it is a bahuvrīhi qualifying 'garbhiṇī'. GROUPING: 106 and 107 appear to be one reasoning ('for ... therefore').

hindi: इसलिए विशेष रूप से उसकी रक्षा, गर्भ को हानि पहुँचाने वालों से, प्रिय और हितकर दोनों से करनी चाहिए।
english: Therefore one should protect her especially, by the pleasant and beneficial (ones), from those that cause injury to the embryo.
notes: 'priyahitābhyām' is the instrumental dual of a dvandva, read 'by the pleasant and the beneficial (ones)'; the nouns are not in the text. 'garbhopaghātakarebhyaḥ' = from those (things) that harm the embryo (the following units list them).

hindi: जैसे-जैसे गर्भ वृद्धि को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे-वैसे भार, आहार और अपचार से, अनुमानित पाठ पर, स्त्री के बल का क्षय होता है।
english: As the embryo reaches growth, so, from the burden, the food and the error (apacāra), on a conjectural reading, there is loss of the woman's strength.

lines_deva: स्त्री हि मूलमपत्यानां स्त्री हि रक्षति रक्षिता
lines_iast: strī hi mūlamapatyānāṃ strī hi rakṣati rakṣitā

hindi: जरायु से मुख ढके होने पर और कफ से कण्ठ लिपटे होने पर और वायु के मार्ग के रुक जाने से गर्भ में रहने वाला रोता नहीं।
english: When the mouth is covered by the jarāyu (fetal membrane) and the throat is enveloped by Kapha, and because of obstruction of the path of wind (vāyu), the one staying in the womb does not cry out.
notes: [02.02.149] Two locative absolutes; the sentence completes in 150 (150 appears to complete it; not stated by the print). jarāyu = the membrane enclosing the fetus (the exact structure, amnion or chorion, is not given). 'cakaphaveṣṭite' = ca kapha-veṣṭite. [02.02.150] Completes the sentence begun in 149 (appears to). 'garbhastha' = the one in the womb (not further specified). 'vāyu' is the wind or air; it is read as wind/air rather than the humour Vāta, though the text does not exclude the latter.

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भावक्रान्ति यानी गर्भ का अवतरण नामक द्वितीय अध्याय
english: Thus the second chapter, named Garbhāvakrānti (the descent of the embryo).
notes: Colophon. The printed tokens 'itigarbhāvakrāṃtirnāma' and 'dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ' are run together by sandhi.
